part.name: Rounded-rectangle frame / bezel ring
part.description: Single-piece rectangular ring with radiused corners and stepped/landed planar faces. Geometry appears as a thin frame in Y (thickness direction) with inner window opening, outer perimeter wall, inner perimeter wall, and two fillet systems (small r=2 edge breaks and larger r=10 corner/edge rounds).
part.symmetry_note: Overall geometry is symmetric about the mid-planes in X and Z (left-right and top-bottom) with repeated corner features at 4 corners.

Section.name: Outer perimeter wall (straight + corner arcs)
features included: Four outer corner arc walls (rounded rectangle corners)
Two outer straight side walls (left and right)
Section.function intent: Defines the external envelope for packaging and provides the primary outer locating boundary when the frame is nested in a housing or surrounded by another component.
Section.physical behavior: Acts as a continuous closed hoop; carries in-plane loads around the perimeter (membrane action) and provides bending stiffness against out-of-plane warping by keeping the section closed.
Section.geometry: Two planar straight wall segments at constant X (left/right) connected by four cylindrical corner wall patches (outer corner radius).
Section.location: Outermost boundary around the full frame opening; includes the extreme X extents and all outer corner regions.

major_faces.description: Cylindrical outer corner wall patch (R≈63) at the opposite upper corner of the outer rounded-rectangle.

Section.name: Inner perimeter wall (window boundary)
features included: Two inner straight side walls (left and right)
Four inner corner arc walls (rounded rectangle inner corners)
Section.function intent: Provides the functional aperture/opening, clearance for an inserted component (e.g., screen/glass/insert), and an inner locating boundary.
Section.physical behavior: Closed inner boundary stabilizes the ring section; resists local deformation around the opening and reacts contact forces from an inserted part via compression on the inner wall.
Section.geometry: Two planar straight wall segments at constant X (inner left/right) connected by four cylindrical corner wall patches (inner corner radius).
Section.location: Inboard boundary of the frame; surrounds the central window opening.

Section.name: Primary broad face (Side A) with window cutout
features included: Main planar face on one side of the frame
Planar annulus with inner opening (wire cutout)
Section.function intent: Provides a primary seating/sealing/mounting face against a mating component; acts as a reference surface for assembly stack-up.
Section.physical behavior: Carries compressive contact pressure when clamped; provides bending stiffness as a flange-like surface connecting outer and inner perimeter walls.
Section.geometry: Large planar annular surface (plane with inner boundary), spanning nearly the full perimeter footprint.
Section.location: One of the two largest opposing faces of the frame (one side of the thickness).

major_faces.name: Side A main annular face
major_faces.description: Large plane face with an inner cutout loop; primary broad face on Side A.

Section.name: Secondary broad face (Side B) / step face with window cutout
features included: Opposing planar face on the other side of the frame
Smaller planar annulus/step with inner opening (wire cutout)
Section.function intent: Provides the opposing seating face and/or a stepped land for spacing, gasket preload control, or a cosmetic reveal.
Section.physical behavior: Acts as the second flange face; resists clamp loads from the opposite direction and completes the closed-section stiffness in combination with Side A.
Section.geometry: Planar annular face (with inner boundary), parallel/near-parallel to Side A but offset in thickness; smaller area suggests a step/land region.
Section.location: Opposite side of the thickness from S3 (other major side).

major_faces.name: Side B annular/step face
major_faces.description: Plane face with an inner cutout loop; secondary broad/step face on Side B.

Section.name: Top/Bottom planar lands (axial flats / seat bands)
Section.function intent: Provides flat lands for seating, spacing, or controlled contact at the top and bottom regions; may define a stop surface for assembly.
Section.physical behavior: Transfers localized compressive loads and spreads them into the ring; provides geometric datum bands for inspection/fixturing.
Section.geometry: Four planar rectangular bands near minimum and maximum Z extents (two at bottom region, two at top region).
Section.location: Near the Z-min and Z-max of the part, spanning long straight segments across X.

major_faces.description: Secondary planar band near the lower Z region; likely adjacent to a fillet/chamfer transition.

major_faces.description: Planar band near the upper Z region; long straight segment across X.

major_faces.name: Top inner/secondary land plane
major_faces.description: Secondary planar band near the upper Z region; likely adjacent to a fillet/chamfer transition.

Section.name: Small-radius edge breaks / blend network (r≈2)
features included: Small edge fillets along long straight runs
Small corner blends (torus) connecting straight fillets to corner arcs
Small cylindrical blends along short side runs
Section.function intent: Reduces stress concentrations, removes sharp edges for handling, and improves manufacturability (molding/printing/finishing).
Section.physical behavior: Smooths curvature transitions; reduces peak contact stress and increases fatigue resistance by increasing local radius at edges.
Section.geometry: A network of small cylinders (R=2) and small tori (minor R=2) around multiple perimeter edges and corners.
Section.location: Distributed around perimeter edges where planar and cylindrical faces meet; present at both inner/outer boundaries and at top/bottom transitions.

Section.name: Large-radius rounds (r≈10) at primary perimeter edges
features included: Large edge rounds along long straight runs
Section.function intent: Provides robust corner/edge rounding for strength, safety, and improved flow/finish (e.g., injection molding radii).
Section.physical behavior: Reduces notch sensitivity and distributes stress over larger curvature; improves impact resistance at corners and reduces local peak strain.
Section.geometry: Cylinders (R=10) along long and side runs plus corner tori (minor R=10) forming large-radius transitions.
Section.location: Predominantly on the outer/primary visible perimeter edges and corners, surrounding the frame footprint.
